subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue these as separate native/core contracts, plugin/SDK extensions, or decline any of the three requested tracks for now?
rationale: The request adds new tool schemas, context/session lifecycle semantics, and optional plan-gating config; automation cannot choose those product and compatibility boundaries safely.

options.title: Split Into Three Design Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for native batching, context block lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Route Optional Pieces To Plugins
options.body: Allow plugin or skill implementations for batching or memory-like behavior and only add core SDK seams if the current extension points are proven insufficient.

options.title: Decline Plan Enforcement
options.body: Keep update_plan as advisory progress tracking and explicitly reject strict runner-enforced plan gating as too much orchestration policy for core.

recommendation.title: Split Into Three Design Tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella and require separate maintainer-reviewed designs for native batching, context block lifecycle, and plan enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the strongest adjacent history across update_plan, strict-agentic behavior, web tool schema, and the previous keep-open product review.
